Rashi on Berakhot 58a:10:1.hebrew: חצבי לנהרא - הכדין השלמים הולכים לנהר לשאוב מים:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:10:1.english: Jugs to the river - The intact jugs go to the river to draw water.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:10:2.hebrew: כגני לייא - השבורים להיכן, כלומר: למה הולכים? ואף אתה, שאתה סומא ולא תראהו, להיכן תלך:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:10:2.english: Where do the broken [jugs] go? - The broken [ones], to where [are they going]? That is to say: Why are they going? And you too, since you are blind and will not see him, where are you going?

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:12:1.english: [They] gouged out his eyes - They gouged out his eyes.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:14:1.english: And lovers of justice - [That is,] lovers of justice.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:14:2.english: A staff - A staff with which to chastise.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:15:1.hebrew: התורה אמרה אם בא להרגך השכם להרגו - אם במחתרת וגו' (שמות כב). לפי שבא על עסקי נפשות — שיודע הוא שאם ימצא ותמצאנו חותר, לא תעמיד עצמך מלהציל ממונך, והוא בא לדעת כן, שיקום עליך ויהרגך — אמרה תורה: השכם אתה והרגהו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:15:1.english: The Torah said: “If one comes to kill you, kill him first” - “[If a thief is found] tunneling, etc.” (Exodus 22:1). Because he comes with lethal intent — for he knows that if he is found and you find him tunneling, you will not restrain yourself from saving your property, and he comes with this intention, that he will rise against you and kill you — the Torah said: “You, kill him first.”

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:1.hebrew: הממלכה זו מלחמת עמלק - דכתיב בה כסא מלכות: כי יד על כס יה (שמות י״ז:ט״ז), כלומר: על ידי מלחמה ליי' בעמלק יתעלה כסאו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:1.english: “The kingdom” — this is the war of Amalek - For regarding it, a royal throne is written: “For a hand is upon the throne of the Lord” (Exodus 17:16) — that is to say, through the war for the Lord against Amalek, His throne will be exalted.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:2.hebrew: המתנשא - מדכתיב לשון נשיאות, משמע על נשיא ראש משך ותובל:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:2.english: And You are exalted - Since it is written in the language of princeship [nesi'ut], it implies [that it refers to] the "chief prince of Meshech and Tubal."

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:3.hebrew: לכל לראש - לכל הקם להיות לראש, הוא מתנשא — כלומר, שהוא גוזר ומעמידו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:3.english: As head above all - Over anyone who arises to be a leader, He [God] is exalted — that is to say, that He decrees and appoints him.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:4.hebrew: ריש גרגיתא - בור. הממונה על החופרין חפירות למלאותן מים, כדי להשקות בהן שדותיהן:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:16:4.english: The head of a cistern - [A gargita is] a cistern. [The "head" is] the one appointed over those who dig pits to fill them with water in order to irrigate their fields with them.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:1:1.hebrew: נתקללה בבל נתקללו שכניה - כלומר: אוי לרשע, אוי לשכנו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:1:1.english: [When] Babylonia was cursed, its neighbors were cursed - That is to say: "Woe to the wicked, woe to his neighbor."

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:1:2.hebrew: קאת וקפוד - חיות ועופות רעים, ומזיקין את השכנים. אבל עי השדה ומטעי כרם שנתקללו בה ערי ישראל — הנאה היא לשכנים:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:1:2.english: Pelican and hedgehog - [These are] harmful beasts and birds, and they harm the neighbors. But “a heap in the field” and “plantings of a vineyard,” with which the cities of Israel were cursed — [this] is a benefit to the neighbors.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:2:1.hebrew: אוכלוסי - חיל גדול של ששים רבוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:2:1.english: Multitudes - A large host of sixty myriad [600,000].

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:2:2.hebrew: חכם הרזים - היודע מה שבלב כל אלו:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:2:2.english: Knower of secrets - The One Who knows what is in the heart of all of these.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:3:1.hebrew: לשמשני - שהם חורשים וזורעים, ואני מוצא מוכן:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:3:1.english: To serve me - For they plow and sow, and I find [it] prepared.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:4:1.hebrew: כל אומות שוקדות ובאות לפתחי - עשיר היה, והכל באין אצלו לסחורה:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:4:1.english: All nations diligently come to my entrance - He was wealthy, and all come to him for commerce.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:9:1.hebrew: שאם יזכה - לעולם הבא, ויראה בכבוד מלך המשיח:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:9:1.english: That if he will merit - [To enter] the World to Come, and see the glory of King Messiah.

Rashi on Berakhot 58a:9:2.hebrew: יבחין - כמה יתר כבוד נוטלי שכר מצות, יותר ממה שהיה כבוד האומות בעוה"ז:
Rashi on Berakhot 58a:9:2.english: He will distinguish - How much greater is the glory of those who receive the reward of the mitzvot than what the glory of the nations was in this world.
